topics.label: Introduction to the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and sets expectations regarding the complexity and importance of the complement system.

topics.label: Overview, nomenclature, and central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the overall structure, historical naming conventions, and the central role of C3 cleavage in complement activation.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the upstream recognition mechanisms that drive complement activation and converge on a local threshold concentration of C3b.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream effector processes triggered by complement activation to eliminate pathogens and amplify inflammation.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the regulatory proteins that protect host cells from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how genetic or acquired deficiencies in distinct complement components result in specific clinical diseases.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the evolutionary adaptations pathogens use to evade complement-mediated destruction, using Staphylococcus aureus as a primary model.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the discussion on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
